title: Two-Factor Authentication
description: Simulate a pixel display responding to rect and rotation instructions.
writeup:
## Approach

The puzzle simulates a tiny monochrome display that starts with all pixels off. The input consists of three types of instructions: drawing a filled rectangle, rotating a row, and rotating a column. The task is to apply all instructions and determine how many pixels are lit (Part 1) and what message appears on the screen (Part 2).

The display is represented as a 2D grid of booleans or characters. Each instruction mutates the grid. The operations are simple but must be applied carefully, especially the wraparound behavior of rotations.

## Part 1

We initialize a 50×6 grid of off pixels. For each instruction:
- `rect AxB` turns on all pixels in the rectangle from (0,0) to (A-1,B-1).
- `rotate row y=A by B` shifts row A to the right by B, wrapping around.
- `rotate column x=A by B` shifts column A downward by B, wrapping around.

After processing all instructions, we count the number of lit pixels.

## Part 2

The final screen forms a blocky ASCII-style message. We simply render the grid row by row. The puzzle expects you to visually read the letters.

The logic is identical to Part 1; only the output changes.
